headline: Submarine Cables: The Ocean's Invisible Internet Backbone
summary: TeleGeography's submarine cable map reveals how fiber-optic cables physically carry global internet traffic. Hyperscalers now fund private cables to control latency and redundancy, reshaping cloud region strategy for engineers.

slides.title: The Ocean's Invisible Internet Backbone
slides.subtitle: Submarine cables carry 99% of intercontinental data traffic.
slides.body: TeleGeography's map reveals the physical infrastructure powering global connectivity. How do these cables shape cloud performance and redundancy?
slides.deep_dive: Hundreds of fiber-optic cables crisscross oceans, linking continents. Each cable contains multiple fiber pairs, using repeaters to boost signals across thousands of kilometers. Landing stations connect to terrestrial networks, forming the backbone of cloud regions and global internet exchange points.
slides.key_fact: Submarine cables are the physical layer of the global internet, not satellites.
slides.why_it_matters: Cloud region latency and resilience depend on cable routes and landing points.

slides.title: Exploding Demand Drives New Cable Construction
slides.body: Cloud adoption, video streaming, and AI workloads surge bandwidth needs. Hyperscalers now fund private cables to control latency, cost, and redundancy.

_story.title: The Ocean's Invisible Internet Backbone
_story.hook: Did You Know the internet travels across oceans on cables thicker than a garden hose, buried deep underwater? 🤯
_story.headline: The Massive Engineering Behind Your Instant Global Connection
_story.fact_summary: Every time you video call someone across the world or stream a movie from another continent, your data isn't just flying through the air. It's actually zipping through massive fiber optic cables, some as thick as a garden hose, lying on the ocean floor, sometimes buried deep to protect them from anchors and even shark bites. These incredible underwater highways are powered by electricity and span tens of thousands of miles, making our instant global communication possible, truly a marvel of human ingenuity hidden beneath the waves.
